discipline: AEAL — every finding cites a manuscript line range or section label. The posture is adversarial-to-self: test each Lecerf objection for merit, do not defend.

objection_1_assessment.objection: The paper is very difficult to read.

findings.finding: The abstract is a single unbroken ~35-line paragraph (L78-L113) carrying 12+ specialist terms before any are introduced: 'Edge-Borel object', 'Borel normalization', 'p-curvature', 'Andre-Chudnovsky-Katz trichotomy', 'pseudo-reflection', 'Aschbacher classification', 'exponential torus', 'determining factors', 'connection coefficient'. Wall-of-text density.

Main result IS stated early — SL_4 appears in the abstract (L96) and again in the R1-R6 results list on p2 (R4, L171). So the readability problem is NOT 'result buried'; it is density/signposting. This partially mitigates the objection.

No explicit roadmap paragraph ('Section 2 establishes ..., Section 3 ...'). The R1-R6 list (L162-179) gives section pointers per result and is a partial substitute, but there is no narrative structure guide for a non-specialist.

Forward references to undefined objects in the first 3 pages: 'exponential torus' used in abstract/intro but only described at L384-387; 'connection coefficient' used at L101/L126 but only defined at L557-560; 'determining factors' used before eq (3) at L227; 'p-curvature', 'Aschbacher classification', 'ACK trichotomy' used with no in-paper definition.
findings.evidence: abstract L78-113; intro L120-199; vs definitions at L227, L384-387, L557-560

findings.finding: Sentence-level density: the central SL_4 sentence in the abstract (L94-L100) runs ~7 lines with stacked subordinate clauses; the 'what these results do not give' sentence (L105-L109) runs ~5 lines. Several body sentences exceed 4 lines.

objection_1_assessment.summary: VALID but not catastrophic. The result is stated early; the difficulty is the wall-of-text abstract, absent roadmap, and forward-referencing of undefined specialist vocabulary. Fixable by restructuring, not rewriting the mathematics.

objection_2_assessment.objection: Central objects are not defined properly.
objection_2_assessment.structural_fact: The 786-line manuscript contains ZERO \begin{definition} environments. Every central object is introduced inline in prose; several are introduced only by citation to the author's own EBR-I/EBR-II preprints.

per_object_table.definition_quality: CITATION-ONLY in intro / DEFERRED RIGOROUS later

per_object_table.first_definition: L359-372 as 'organizing vocabulary'; descriptions only inside the elimination table L483-505

objection_2_assessment.notation_consistency: Stable internally (theta, R, gamma, chi, M_0/M_R, exp_0/exp_R consistent). The prior internal referee pass (EBR3_referee_findings.md F1) already corrected an Aschbacher C5/C6/C8 numbering slip; no competing conventions remain unreconciled. So the defect is missing/citation-only definitions, not inconsistent ones.
objection_2_assessment.summary: VALID. The objection is well-founded for the EBR-specific objects (the EBR construction and the connection coefficient are used in the abstract but are only citation-resolvable to the author's own preprints, not self-contained), and for the total absence of Definition environments. It is weaker for L_2 (rigorously given) and for standard objects a specialist would know — but Lecerf is a computer-algebra generalist, for whom 'defined via my earlier preprint' reads as not-defined.

objection_3_assessment.objection: The main result does not seem sufficiently significant.
objection_3_assessment.verdict: FRAMING-PROBLEM (primary); BOTH (a genuine substance-narrowness caps top-tier suitability)

findings.finding: Main theorem (thm:main, L507-513) computes G_Gal(L_2)^circ = SL_4 for ONE specific operator (d=2, b(n)=3n^2+n+1). The statement is a single-instance Galois-group identification.

Significance is framed ENTIRELY inside the author's own EBR program ('continues the EBR program', 'fix the smallest non-rigid case', L120-134). For an outside reader there is no motivation that does not route through EBR-I/II. No external 'why this matters'.

No comparison to the nearest PRIOR result outside the program and no explicit improvement claim against the general differential-Galois-computation literature (no Compoint-Singer, van Hoeij-Weil, Singer-Ulmer, Hartmann). The only comparison is to EBR-II (self).

The marquee motivating question — transcendence of the connection coefficient — is explicitly LEFT OPEN (L181-199, L697, L707-711, L726-730). The delivered payoff is (a) one operator's Galois group, (b) a non-Liouvillian corollary, (c) a numeric non-elementarity null. A reader expecting the headline question may read the delivered result as a way-station.

UNDERPLAYED significance hook: there is no complete push-button algorithm/CAS routine for the differential Galois group of an order-4 operator WITH an irregular singularity (Kovacic is order-2 only; CAS support stops at factorization/structural hints). This paper does it completely and unconditionally with a priori degree bounds making the searches complete, plus four machine-checked Lean cores. That is a genuine methodological contribution the paper never advertises as such.
findings.evidence: method in sec:main L354-528, sec:bounds L463-477, sec:lean L644-661; never framed against SOTA

objection_3_assessment.distinguish: Primarily a FRAMING-PROBLEM: a complete, bound-complete, partly-Lean-verified Galois computation for an irregular-singular order-4 operator is a real contribution, but it is presented as 'result 4 of 6 about one operator in my program' with the headline question left open and zero SOTA positioning. There is a residual SUBSTANCE component (single instance, general d open) that legitimately caps suitability for a generalist top-tier venue but NOT for a computational venue (JSC/AAECC) where a complete worked method + formalization is squarely in scope.
objection_3_assessment.summary: FRAMING-dominant. Reframe as a methodology (complete order-4 irregular-singular Galois computation with verified completeness bounds + formal cores) positioned against what CAS/SOTA cannot currently do, and the significance objection largely dissolves for a computational venue. Tightly coupled to Objection 4.

objection_4_assessment.objection: It would have been useful to comment on what can be done by computer algebra systems and state-of-the-art algorithms.

findings.finding: Keyword scan of the full source: ZERO occurrences of Magma, GAP, Sage, Maple, Mathematica, Singular. 'computer algebra' appears only as an evidence-grade descriptor (L157 'verified by hand and computer algebra', L305 'computer algebra and hand argument'). No complexity analysis, no benchmarking, no SOTA section.

The paper is AWARE of the relevant tool but never discusses it: 'an independent DFactor-style confirmation was unavailable on the host' (L306-307) and 'neither relies on a decision-procedure factorization' (L320-321). DFactor (Maple DEtools, van Hoeij factorization) is named in passing and dropped.

This is the editor's own professional centre of mass (Lecerf, EiC of a computer-algebra journal). For AAECC/JSC the absence of any CAS/SOTA context is the single most concrete and most damaging gap — and simultaneously the most actionable.
findings.evidence: venue scope (AAECC/JSC); cover letter L56-70 positions the work as 'algorithmic/computer-algebra' yet the manuscript never engages CAS

candidate_cas_sota_comparisons_to_addres: Kovacic's algorithm is order-2 only (already cited [Kovacic]); state explicitly that no order-4 analogue with a completeness guarantee exists. [VERIFY primary in Stage 4]

Maple DEtools[DFactor] / DFactorsols (van Hoeij factorization): what it decides (reducibility/factorization) vs what this paper needs (the full identity component); the paper's L306 note that DFactor was unavailable should become an explicit CAS-capability paragraph. [VERIFY primary Maple docs in Stage 4]

Compoint-Singer 'Computing Galois groups of linear differential equations' (LNCS, 2008) and van Hoeij-Weil reduction methods: the relevant SOTA framework for the group itself; missing from the bibliography entirely. [VERIFY DOI/venue in Stage 4]
Singer-Ulmer / Hartmann (order-3 and reductive-group methods): boundary of what is algorithmically settled below order 4. [VERIFY in Stage 4]

Statement that the paper's contribution is precisely to do, completely and with a priori degree bounds (sec:bounds L463-477), a computation that current CAS tools do not perform push-button for an irregular-singular order-4 operator — turning Objection 4 into a significance argument for Objection 3.

Reproducibility/CAS-replicability: which sub-results (p-curvature, factor exclusion, invariant-form searches, primitivity searches) ARE replicable in standard CAS and how (the repro bundle scripts), so a referee can re-run them. [list the scripts already in ebr3_repro.zip]
objection_4_assessment.summary: ABSENT and VALID at HIGH severity for the venue class. The fix is bounded and well-scoped (one new ~1-2 pp CAS/SOTA subsection + ~4-6 new citations) and doubles as the cure for Objection 3's framing component.

halt_gate_2.condition: All four objections INVALID or PARTIALLY-INVALID with minor severity -> halt (possible self-defense bias).
halt_gate_2.reason: Not all-invalid. Objections 1, 2, 4 are VALID (4 at HIGH severity); 3 is a real FRAMING problem with a substance component. The assessment finds genuine merit, not a defense.

halt_gate_3.condition: Any objection VALID with HIGH severity -> flag for operator (revision may be larger than a normal pass).
halt_gate_3.flag: Objection 4 is VALID/ABSENT at HIGH severity (total gap, editor's core concern). Objection 2 carries HIGH-severity sub-items (EBR construction and connection coefficient are citation-only yet used in the abstract). HOWEVER both HIGH findings are well-scoped additive fixes (a CAS/SOTA subsection; a Definitions/Preliminaries section), not structural rewrites of the mathematics. The revision is larger than a one-paragraph patch but is bounded and does not touch any graded result.
halt_gate_3.operator_action_required: Review the HIGH-severity flags before Stage 4. They inform the Option A/B/C choice at HALT GATE 4.

overall.verdict: Three of four objections VALID (1 MEDIUM, 2 MEDIUM-HIGH, 4 HIGH); objection 3 is a FRAMING problem (MEDIUM) tightly coupled to 4. None of the findings touches a graded mathematical result — all are presentation, definitional self-containment, framing, and missing CAS/SOTA context. The desk-rejection is substantively answerable without redoing the mathematics.
overall.coupling_note: Objections 3 and 4 are the same fix viewed twice: a CAS/SOTA section both supplies the missing computational context (4) and reframes the single-operator theorem as a complete method current tools cannot match (3).
